title: Hegel: Being, Nothing, Becoming
subtitle: A concept that moves on its own
learning_objective: Follow the opening move of Hegel’s Logic: pure being, without any determination, cannot be told apart from nothing — and their truth is the movement of each into the other, becoming. See why this is not a thesis–antithesis–synthesis template.
disclaimer: A simplified reading aid for the opening of Hegel’s Science of Logic, pending content review. Hegel scholars read this passage in different ways.

steps.title: Strip away
steps.prompt: Here is something with many features. Remove every feature, one by one.

steps.title: Judge
steps.prompt: What is left — something, or nothing?

steps.title: Experiment
steps.prompt: Try to name a difference between pure being and pure nothing. Then watch the two.

steps.title: Judge again
steps.prompt: Pure being and pure nothing — what is their relation?

steps.title: Explain
steps.prompt: What Hegel claims — and what he doesn’t.

steps.title: Apply
steps.prompt: Follow a concept of your own through an inner tension.

steps.title: Keep
steps.prompt: Keep what you understood and what you still wonder about.

feedback_rules.say: Every feature is gone. What remains has no ‘what’ at all — Hegel calls it pure being.
You say something remains: pure being. Next: can you say how it differs from nothing?
You say nothing remains. Hold on — next you’ll see why Hegel finds both answers right.
‘I can’t tell’ is exactly where Hegel’s Logic begins.
Each difference you name brings back a feature you removed.
Being vanishes into nothing, nothing into being — ceasing-to-be and coming-to-be. Hegel calls this movement becoming.
That is close to Hegel: their truth is the movement of each into the other — becoming.
Hegel agrees they can’t be told apart — and adds that they are still not simply the same: each passes over into the other.
Try to say how — every difference you named brought back a feature.

differences.reply: ‘Exists’ already says more than pure being: it adds a determination (being there, being something). Pure being has none.

differences.text: Being has some content; nothing is empty.
differences.reply: Which content? Every content you name is a determination you just stripped away. Pure being is just as empty.

differences.text: I can think of being, but not of nothing.
differences.reply: Try it: thinking pure being, with no ‘what’ at all, is thinking nothing in particular — the same emptiness.

differences.text: Being is positive, nothing is negative.
differences.reply: ‘Positive’ and ‘negative’ are themselves determinations. Without them, the two can’t be told apart.

layers.title: ① Being, nothing, becoming
layers.body: Hegel’s Logic begins with pure being: with no determination at all, it is ‘in fact nothing’. Pure nothing, thought through, is the same empty thought. Their truth is the movement in which each has already passed into the other — becoming, as coming-to-be and ceasing-to-be.
layers.source: Hegel, Science of Logic (1812/1832), Doctrine of Being, ch. 1; Encyclopaedia Logic §§86–88 — check against your edition
layers.maps_to: Stripping the features · watching the two

layers.title: ② Not thesis–antithesis–synthesis
layers.body: Hegel did not present his method as ‘thesis–antithesis–synthesis’; that formula is linked more with Fichte and later popular summaries. The point is that a concept, thought through, turns into another by itself (immanently) — not that a third idea is added from outside.
layers.source: See e.g. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, “Hegel’s Dialectics”

layers.title: ③ An open debate
layers.body: What this opening proves, and how to read it, is debated among scholars. This experiment is a reading aid: it lets you feel the move, not decide what it means for all of Hegel.

content.map_note: Watch for concepts that change by thinking them through — not because someone adds a new idea.

apply_fields.label: What I first thought it meant
What it became — what is kept, what changed
